findings.evidence: Core Prompt v2.7 required role and memory isolation but did not bind provider/model identity. The shared adapter consequently allowed all roles, including Challenger, to inherit one optional global Codex model.
findings.minimal_revision: Bind each model-bearing role to its approved provider/model, require new ephemeral executions, forbid Challenger fallback to Codex, and fail closed as PLATFORM_LIMITATION when an exact binding is unavailable.
findings.compatibility: Existing v2.7/v0.8 runs retain their frozen prompt authority. New runs use v2.8/v0.9.
regression_scenarios: Developer launches gpt-6-astra in an ephemeral Codex execution.
Reviewer launches gpt-5.6-sol without Developer conversation state.
Challenger launches deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash through a read-only external adapter and cannot fall back to Codex.
Adjudicator launches gpt-6-astra without Developer conversation state.
Missing Challenger credentials stop as PLATFORM_LIMITATION before human confirmation.
Mastra and LangGraph resolve identical role execution bindings.
